newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SAB merges, recapitalises Hungarian units.
newsitem.headline: SAB merges, recapitalises Hungarian units.

text.p: South African Breweries said on Tuesday it had merged its two Hungarian breweries under the name of Dreher Sorgyarak Rt and recapitalised by $54 million.
"These two companies have been financially and legally merged," Alan Richards, Dreher Sorgyarak Rt's chairman, told a news conference. The merger is effective as of today.
"The reasons for merging our two companies are really very simple. From the beginning we've been determined to create one family and one set of aspirations for our people."
The opening share capital of Dreher Sorgyarak is 13.09 billion forints and the company has around 38 percent of the market in Hungary, Dreher said in a statement.
Richards said Hungary's new Competition Act, effective since January, had cleared the way for the move.
"The new competition act...allows for mergers of this type," Richards said, answering Reuters' question on how the Competition Office would react to this high market share.
"It specifically allows for the merger of companies which have common international ownership," he added.
Richards said Dreher expected to sell 2.7 million hectolitres of beer in 1997, generating $120 million in turnover and $7 million in operating profit.

This compares to combined sales volume in 1994, soon after SAB purchased the companies, of 3.4-3.5 million hectolitres, he said. The Hungarian beer market had shrunk some 30 percent since 1991 but had started to recover, he added.
The freshly injected capital of $54 million almost equals the amount SAB originally paid for the two breweries, Richards said.

Of the total, $29 million was used to eliminate all existing debt, $15 million will be spent on further investments in sales and marketing, $5 million to update information technology and another $5 million will be added to the working capital.
SAB bought an 80.4 percent stake in Kobanyai in 1993 for $50 million, spending half of this amount for a capital increase. In 1994 it bought the total of the indebted Kanizsai brewery for $8 million.
With the investment, SAB's stake in the new companies rises above 97 percent, with the rest divided between Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt and local governments of Budapest.
SAB is the second foreign brewery to merge its Hungarian units. Earlier this year Austria's Brau Union AG merged the since delisted Elso Magyar Szovetkezeti Sorgyar Rt and Soproni Sorgyar Rt.
